title: Contraction-free intuitionistic propositional sequents: G4ip

based_on.title: Contraction-free sequent calculi for intuitionistic logic: a correction
Constructive Logic (15-317), Lecture 11: G4ip, a contraction-free calculus
based_on.pages: pp.1–9: rules, soundness and numerical weight; corrected completeness taken from Dyckhoff 2018

summary: Replace retained implication-left by G4ip rules, prove a decreasing numerical measure, and transform native intuitionistic certificates in both directions.
abstract: A backward attempt to prove a sequent can repeat the same goal when an implication remains available in its own producer branch. G4ip avoids that loop by choosing a different left rule for each possible shape of an implication’s input. We derive these rules in ordinary intuitionistic logic and give a numerical weight that decreases at every backward premise. A proof transformation then shows that the specialized rules still prove every intuitionistic sequent. The construction keeps native negation and finite assumptions connected to the existing calculus, while explaining why the absence of a contraction rule does not restrict how often an assumption may be used.
